Resolves #18554

A worker error that a component catches and logs fails nothing, which is how #18551 shipped with every check green. The mirror (#18557, #18567) already put SharedWorker `console.error` and `onerror` on the page, but nothing read it, and an unhandled rejection never reached it. This PR forwards unhandled rejections and adds a gate to the shared e2e fixture that fails a test whose page receives a worker error or an uncaught page error it did not name, whether the error was mirrored from a SharedWorker or logged by a dedicated worker. It also fixes the eight defects the gate found: four in `colors/tearOutMatrix`, two in the component tier, one in the portal, and one in how the AI client's socket reports an absent bridge.

Evidence: L3 achieved (hosted `workflow_dispatch` runs on the tier's own runner — red-first on the forward, the gate's controls, the tier inventoried with the gate on, and each defect red under the gate, then green) → L3 required (the ACs are about what CI observes).

## Deltas from ticket

- **The eight defects the gate found are fixed here, not ticketed.**
  - `DashboardSortZone#calculateExpandedLayout` threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'flex')`. `Container#onDragBoundaryExit` moves the dragged widget into its popup before `startWindowDrag` lays out the rest, so `owner.items[indexMap[i]]` read past the shortened array. `container.SortZone` now keeps `ownerItems`, the drag-start snapshot `indexMap` indexes into, set wherever `indexMap` is built; a unit arm fails with that TypeError on the old lookup. Run E shows why both drag paths need it: set only on the remote path, every local window drag failed at the first slot.
  - A closing tear-out window left `Worker port disconnected before reply` errors, four of them unhandled rejections. `worker.Base#removePort` names the rejection `PortDisconnectedError`; `Neo.mjs` treats an unhandled one like `Neo.isDestroyed`, and `App#onConnect` no longer logs it. The message is unchanged, as `ReplyLoss.spec` pins.
  - Run F failed row 2 once on `vdom update failed neo-dragproxycontainer-1 … Component not found for id: neo-grid-body-1__row-8`. A child destroyed out of its parent's render tree without an update (`destroy(true, true)`) stayed named in the parent's stored vnode until the parent's next update landed, and an ancestor flight in that window resolved the name strictly. A plain container reproduces it. `component.Base#destroy` now unlinks the reference: the node stays as the vnode the child last rendered, so the parent's next update removes it, or diffs a newcomer with the same id against it. The landing boundary (`VdomLifecycle#syncVnodeTree`) unlinks as well; it used to prune, which left the node in the DOM for good. `grid.Row#destroy` stops swallowing its base's arguments, so a row retired through that shared path behaves like any other child; the row pool itself takes the batched route below.
  - `VDom Worker: [RemoteMethodAccess] Reply not routable (no live port)` appeared once in run E and was the only failure in runs G and H, row 2 twice each. The probe below showed the path. The request, `Neo.vdom.Helper.updateBatch` for a closing popup, arrived over the App–VDom channel with no source port, while the popup's port, its reply's only route, was already retired. `worker.Base` now keeps the 16 most recent windows whose port it retired, and `sendReply` stays silent for those. The caller settles too: `promiseMessage` records the window a request is for, `removePort` rejects a portless request with `PortDisconnectedError` once that window's last port retires, and the flight treats that rejection as teardown. A reply to a window the worker never knew still logs; `ReplyLoss.spec` pins all three.
  - `layout.Card#afterSetActiveIndex` threw `Trying to activate a non existing card` for a tab container created without cards. Both the layout's construction and `tab.Container`'s constructed hook activated index 0 over an empty items array. An empty container now has nothing to activate; an out-of-range index into a container that holds cards still throws. Four `CardGridContainment` arms surfaced it.
  - `grid.header.Toolbar#passSizeToBody` read `columnPositions` from a null body: its body getter resolves nothing once the toolbar has no grid. `SplitterHeavyContent` reaches that through `grid.Container#onResize`, in the arm that destroys and remounts its grids. The method now returns when there is no body.
  - The portal's three `onIntersect` handlers passed `store.get(recordId)` straight to `selectionModel.select`. A section that intersected after its record had left the store reached `list.Base#getItemRecordId(null)`: `LearnLinkRoutingNL` failed 1 of 1 in CI and 2 of 3 in the gated tier run. Each handler now selects only a record the store holds.
  - Once the gate read dedicated workers, `RowPinning.spec` failed through it on `App Worker: Max reconnection attempts reached`. An app that sets `useAiClient` starts the Neural Link client, which gives up after five attempts when no bridge listens, about 15 s after boot, so only a long arm outlives it. `ai.Client#onSocketError` already reports an absent bridge as a warning; the give-up was the one path still logged as an error, by `data.connection.WebSocket` itself. The socket now fires `reconnectFailed` with a `handled` flag and logs the error only when no owner sets it, and the client warns and sets it. A give-up nobody handles is still an error, whether or not someone listened.
- **A shrinking row pool leaves the stored vnode in one walk** (operator challenge, @tobiu, on the bulk retirement above). Per retired row, `destroy(true, …)` did two things a contraction does not need: its parent-vdom edit is redundant, because `createRowPool` rebuilds `cn` from the surviving pool immediately after the loop, and its stored-vnode walk ran once per row over a tree that still held the whole pool. The contraction now retires rows with a plain `destroy()` and unlinks the entire retired set in one `VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences(me.vnode, retired)` — the call the map argument exists for. Measured below; the invariant RA-1 asked for is unchanged, and so is whole-body teardown, which still retires rows through `Body#destroy` with the defaults.
- **A ninth defect, found by this gate after review, deliberately NOT fixed here.** @neo-opus-grace's CI met the fixture on its first contact and it caught an unnamed App Worker error in the same `colors` tier: `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'store' of 'grid' as it is null` at `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs:218`. `updateGrid(records)` reads `this.getReference('grid')` and destructures it unguarded, while its only caller is a socket push — so a package arriving before the reference resolves, or after a tear-out destroyed the grid, throws into a handler nobody was failing on. She falsified it as head-correlated before naming it: `dev@8672557760` passed the same job with this fixture already live, her diff is a comment block in a spec that workflow never selects, and a re-run at the identical head went green, so it is intermittent. It is exactly the class this PR exists to make visible, and it is left for its own change because this head is approved and a one-line app guard is not worth spending the reviewing seat's remaining budget on. Recorded here so the merge carries it.
- **The give-up event is renamed** (operator RC). `reconnect_failed` was the only snake_case event name fired anywhere in `src/`, `apps/` or `examples/`, against 135 camelCase `fire()` sites. It shipped unlistened in v11.18.0 (#8177); this branch adds its first consumer and its payload contract, so the name is settled here rather than carried into that contract. No `neomjs` checkout holds a consumer of the old name.
- **The gate records a page error's stack.** The components job named its two page errors and located neither; the recorded line now carries the frames after the message, as a mirrored worker line does.
- **The gate also reads `pageerror`**, which is what the removed handlers watched.
- **The gate reaches the component tier**: the 7 component specs that import `fixtures.mjs`. Their first gated run failed 5 tests on the two page errors above.
- **A comment in `fixtures.mjs` no longer cites a tracker id**: the published archaeology guard scans every changed file, so touching the file surfaced it.
- **Out of scope:** 23 print-only handlers remain in Brain-dependent specs this tier deselects; they import `fixtures.mjs`, so the gate covers them wherever they run. The Neural Link client receives console output and uncaught errors, not rejections. `ThumbDragPause` failed once in the first CI run on its own blank-frame assertion, with no gate line attached; that intermittent belongs to #18439.

**R1, local.** The unit suite passes, 4067 with 2 skipped. On `c18113f10f`, the silent-removal arm throws `Component not found` at its walk, the in-flight arm's next update removes nothing, and the channel-caller arm stays pending. Against the fix, as mutations:

- **Pruning instead of unlinking** passes each walk and fails all three removal arms: the next update removes nothing, and the newcomer gets a structural delta.
- **A bare node instead of the rendered vnode** makes the reuse diff throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'splice')`.
- **`grid.Row#destroy` dropping its arguments** fails the `Pooling.spec` arm on the hosted message, `Component not found for id: neo-grid-body-1__row-8`.
- **The old flight catch** logs the disconnected window.
- **The gate without the dedicated channel** fails the named dedicated arm at its poll.

`WorkerErrorGate` and both mirror specs finish 10 of 10 as expected, and both unnamed worker arms fail at the gate's teardown, not at a precondition. `WebSocket.spec`: a give-up its owner marks handled logs nothing, and one nobody marks is an error whether or not someone listened; on `fb7bdf3d3e` the handled arm logs the error, and with the socket left on the old event name its owner never hears the give-up (1 failed, 1 passed).

**Contraction cost, local** (the operator's challenge). A 205-row pool over 10 columns contracted to 20, both shapes in the same rig, each run guarded by a precondition that the body's stored vnode holds its rows — one run failed that guard outright and produced no numbers rather than flattering ones. |---|---|---|---|---|

| one walk per contraction (at `22a6dfd18f`) | 2.6 / 2.7 / 4.2 | 0 | 2,036 | walkable, 20 references |

`Pooling.spec` and the non-grid `RaceCondition.spec` arms are unchanged and pass 17 of 17 against the batched shape.

Independently measured by @neo-gpt-emmy on the same challenge, arriving at the same shape before seeing this head, and with one count mine did not take — `VDomUtil.find`, the per-row parent-vdom edit's inner walk. Whole-grid teardown, separately probed at `92c83fa5`: one root removal, 14 rows called with default flags, zero unlink walks — that path is untouched by any of this. The contraction: 100 → 10 costs 90 removals, 34,515 `find` calls and 28,755 unlink calls against 0 `find` and 631 unlink batched; 400 → 10 costs 390 removals, 559,065 `find` and 534,105 unlink against 0 and 2,731. Uninstrumented medians over five repetitions each: 6.716 ms → 1.437 ms and 68.478 ms → 4.823 ms, 20 of 20 arms passing, one identical outgoing removal batch either way.

## Evolution

The first reply-side guard keyed on the request's source port. It passed a unit arm built on port delivery and then failed run H unchanged. The probe showed why: App reaches the VDom worker over a direct channel, so that request never has a source port. The guard was dropped from the branch in favour of the retired-window record. Review R1 then showed that silence was not settlement: the caller's promise stayed pending, so the request now settles when its window's last port retires.

The row-pool fix first removed the retired rows' DOM nodes itself and pruned the body's references. R1 reproduced the same stale reference with a plain container, so the repair moved into the component lifecycle. There, pruning is the obvious shortcut and it is wrong: the parent's next update then has nothing to remove. The reference is unlinked instead, and the DOM removal stays with that update.

## Addressed: the bulk-retirement cost challenge

@tobiu's challenge holds, and it found redundant work rather than a missing justification. New head `22a6dfd18f`.

Per retired row, `destroy(true, …)` did two things a pool contraction does not need:

1. **The parent-vdom edit is redundant here.** `createRowPool` ends with `me.getVdomRoot().cn = me.items.map(item => item.createVdomReference())` — the children list is rebuilt from the surviving pool immediately after the loop, so every retired row's reference is dropped there regardless. `removeVdomChild` per row was work the method then threw away.
2. **The stored-vnode walk does not need to be per row.** `VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences(vnode, retired)` already takes a map of retired ids to their last vnodes; the contraction is one walk over a tree that shrinks as it goes, not one walk per row over the full pool.

The contraction now pops each row, records its vnode, retires it with a plain `destroy()`, and unlinks the whole set once. Whole-body teardown is untouched: `Body#destroy` still retires rows through `row.destroy()` with the defaults.

**Measured**, 205-row pool over 10 columns contracted to 20, both shapes in one rig, each run guarded by a precondition that the body's stored vnode actually holds its rows — one run failed that guard and produced no numbers rather than flattering ones:

| shape | ms | parent-vdom edits | vnode node-descents | end state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-row `destroy(true, true)` (`92c83fa524`) | 27.3 / 31.8 / 34.4 | 185 | 189,440 | walkable, 20 references |
| one walk per contraction (`22a6dfd18f`) | 2.6 / 2.7 / 4.2 | 0 | 2,036 | walkable, 20 references |

RA-1's invariant is unchanged — the body's stored vnode stops naming components the registry no longer knows, each kept as the vnode it last rendered, and the next update removes their DOM nodes. `Pooling.spec` (including *a shrinking pool leaves its stored vnode walkable*) and the non-grid `RaceCondition.spec` arms pass 17 of 17 against the new shape.
